<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. IX.|ACCORDING TO S. IOHN.|245}}</noinclude>{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. IX.}}}}}}

{{c|''To show that by his Baptisme (being the Sacrament of illumination or faith) he vvil take avvay the blindnes of the vvorld, he giueth vvith strange ceremonies sight to one borne blinde. 8 By which vvonderful miracle (the attestation of the partie him self and of his parents concurring) first the neighbours, then also the Pharisees them selues are plainely confounded. Yet so obstinate they are, that because it was the Sabboth when he vvrought it, they inferre that he is not of God: yea and throw out of their Synagogue the partie for confessing him. 35 But our Lord receiueth him: 39 and foretelleth by this occasion, the excecation of the Ievves (because of their vvilful obstinacie) and illumination of the Gentils who confesse their ovvne blindnes.''}} {{dropinitial|A|image=Rhemes New Testament 1582 initial A, scrolling foliage with grotesque heads.png|imgsize=140px|fl={{verse|chapter=9|verse=1}}}}ND {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō wenesday in the 4 weeke of Lent.}}{{sc|Iesvs}} passing by, savv a man blinde from his natiuitie: {{verse|chapter=9|verse=2}}† and his disciples asked him, Rabbi, vvho hath sinned, this man, or his parents, that he should be borne blinde? {{verse|chapter=9|verse=3}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Though many infirmities fall for sinne, yet not al. some comming for probation, and some sent that God by the cure thereof may be glorified.}}∷ Neither hath this man sinned, nor his parents: but that the vvorkes of God may be manifested in him. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=4}}† I must vvorke the vvorkes of him that sent me, vvhiles it is day. The night commeth, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ The time of working, and meriting, is in this life: after death we can deserue no more by our deedes, but must onely receiue good or il, according to the difference of workes here.}}∷ vvhen no man can vvorke. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=5}}† As long as I am in the vvorld, I am the light of the vvorld. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=6}}† When he had said these things, he spit on the ground, and {{sup|‖}} made clay of the spettle, and spred the clay vpon his eies, {{verse|chapter=9|verse=7}}† and said to him, Goe, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ This was a figure of Baptisme, to which al men borne in sinne and blindnes are sent for health & sight. ''Ambr. li. 3 c. 2 de Sacramentis''.}}∷ c vvash in the poole of Siloé, vvhich is interpreted, Sent. He vvent therfore, and vvashed: and he came seeing.

{{verse|chapter=9|verse=8}}† Therfore the neighbours, and they vvhich had seen him before, that he vvas a begger, said, Is not this he that sate, and begged? Others said, That this is he. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=9}}† But others, No, not so, but he is like him. But he said, That I am he. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=10}}† They said therfore to him, Hovv vvere thine eies opened? {{verse|chapter=9|verse=11}}† He answered, That man that is called {{sc|Iesvs}}, made clay: and anointed mine eies, and said to me, Goe to the poole of Siloé, and wash. And I vvent, and vvashed, and savv. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=12}}† And they said to him, VVhere is he? He saith, I know not. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=13}}† They bring him that had been blinde, to the Pharisees. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=14}}† And it vvas the Sabboth vvhen {{sc|Iesvs}} made the clay, and opened his eies.

{{verse|chapter=9|verse=15}}† Againe therfore the Pharisees asked him, hovv he savv. But he said to them, He put clay vpon mine eies, & I vvashed: and I see. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=16}}† Certaine therfore of the Pharisees said, This man is not of God, that keepeth not the Sabboth. But others said, Hovv can a man that is a sinner doe these signes? And there<noinclude>{{rh||Hh iij|vvas}}</noinclude>
